statusText: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so there is no observable NQ price path this hour and none anywhere in the 24-hour horizon, which ends at 02:00 UTC on 16 August - still about 20 hours before the reopen. Tail is 9% (low), holding the action at EA_ON and the status green: pathological one-way structure cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. Friday's close, re-verified again this hour from primary sources, supports that reading - the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, mid-range inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 band and about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%, day range 14.18-14.72), 2Y at 4.15% and 10Y at 4.63% on the latest H.15. Stress stays elevated at 45% because the risk backdrop is not calm: the Strait of Hormuz closure is unresolved with Iran publicly refusing to reopen until U.S. behaviour changes, WTI settled at $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent at $88.52 (+1.67%) for a weekly gain above 5%, and fresh overnight reporting has Washington telling Americans to accept higher gasoline prices while Tehran stays defiant. Confidence is 59% (medium-low): everything except the price path is fresh and primary-sourced, but the price path is the one input that matters most and it does not exist this hour. The operative checkpoint remains the Sunday CME reopen, which the danger window brackets.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (9%) alone. No venue is quoting NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint is the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, where two days of accumulated weekend headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure - the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. Gap risk is genuinely two-way: an unprecedented U.S. Iran economic-isolation package is flagged for next week alongside an indefinite blockade, while Iran ties any Hormuz reopening to an end to that blockade and to sanctions relief, and Iran-Oman talks on new strait arrangements are reported close but short of a full reopening. Either thread can move oil and risk appetite before equities can price it. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: Second full night of the CME weekend halt leaves NQ with no live price path anywhere in the 24-hour horizon: Tail holds low at 9% and EA_ON, while Stress stays elevated at 45% on an unresolved day-169 Hormuz closure, a 5%+ weekly crude rally to $82.40 WTI, and fresh U.S.-Iran escalation rhetoric ahead of a sanctions package flagged for next week.
body:
No live price path is available this hour. CME equity-index futures closed for the weekend at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable for the whole of the current 24-hour horizon. Everything below is the last confirmed state plus corroborated news re-verified from primary sources this hour, and that limitation - not a judgement that markets are calm - is what caps Confidence below the solid band.

Last confirmed structure (Friday 14 August U.S. cash session, re-verified this hour on Yahoo Finance): the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, against a 30,084.50 previous close, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 session range and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20. That is a mid-range, orderly finish - a small down day with two-way trade, not a persistent one-way liquidation and not a close pinned to a session extreme. Nothing in it resembles the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that would justify Tail above the low band, which is why Tail stays at 9% rather than being lifted by the volatility backdrop alone.

Cross-asset, all re-verified this hour: VIX closed at 14.25, down 2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and far below its 35.30 52-week high - equity volatility is not corroborating the geopolitical stress. The latest Federal Reserve H.15 (released 14 August, data for 13 August) shows the 2-year at 4.15%, the 10-year at 4.63% and the 30-year at 5.21%; the curve is not signalling a funding or growth discontinuity. Crude is the one genuinely stressed leg: WTI settled at $82.40, up 1.42% on the day, and Brent at $88.52, up 1.67%, capping a weekly gain of more than 5% that snapped a two-week losing streak. Trading Economics attributes the move to increased U.S. economic pressure on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with the IEA warning of deeper global supply deficits - the agency has cut its second-half 2026 global demand forecast by roughly 550 kb/d on strait-related supply-chain disruption. This is the classic Stress-not-Tail configuration the contract describes: an aligned oil/geopolitics leg conflicting with a benign VIX and an unremarkable curve raises Stress, not Tail.

Geopolitics, new developments only: the Hormuz closure is unresolved into its 169th day. Iran continues to state publicly that the strait stays closed until the U.S. corrects its behaviour and lifts the blockade, directly disputing the U.S. claim of total control, with strait traffic near three-month lows. Reuters reporting timed roughly two hours before this run has Iran defiant on the strait while the U.S. president tells Americans to accept high gasoline prices - rhetorical escalation consistent with the existing impasse rather than a new discontinuity. Iran-Oman talks on new commercial-shipping arrangements are reported close to agreement but explicitly short of a full reopening, and Reuters reports no breakthrough on reviving the June interim deal. A further U.S. economic-isolation package is flagged for next week. Ukraine/Russia adds a second supply thread via the drone strike that halted Russian exports at Novorossiysk. None of this is index-transmitted yet: it is oil-transmitted, and equities cannot price any of it until Sunday's reopen.

Calendar: the 24-hour horizon runs to 02:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August and contains no scheduled U.S. macro release whatsoever. The next checkpoint is the Empire State Manufacturing Index on Monday 17 August at 12:30 UTC; the only high-impact item in the verified seven-day window is the FOMC minutes on Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, well outside this horizon. Because no red event sits inside the next 24 hours, Stress is carried by the standing geopolitical and oil backdrop rather than by event anticipation - but it is not allowed to decay to a trivial level, because that backdrop is live and unresolved even while the venue is shut.

Why the scores are where they are: Tail 9% (low) because pathological one-way price path cannot form when no venue is quoting, with the non-zero floor reserved for weekend headline discontinuity expressing as a reopen gap. Stress 45% (elevated) for the unresolved Hormuz closure, the 5%+ weekly crude rally, the confirmed sanctions package next week and the two-way character of the reopen gap. Confidence 59% (medium-low): index level, VIX, 2Y/10Y/30Y, WTI/Brent, the geopolitical thread and the seven-day calendar were all read from primary sources this hour and are mutually consistent, but the NQ price path - the single most important input to a Tail assessment - is structurally unavailable during the halt, and no amount of secondary evidence substitutes for it. dominantMode is mixed: a benign VIX and orderly Friday tape against a stressed oil and geopolitical leg, with no observable path to arbitrate between them.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band. It ran 8-10% through Friday's Asian and European sessions, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the softer July Retail Sales and University of Michigan prints and the Broadcom/Applied Materials drag produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: roughly 23-29% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data and semiconductor news landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% has held for four consecutive hours including this one. Those past opinions are preserved as published. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and has firmed to 56-58% since midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 03:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 02:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly 20 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 9% for the first eighteen slots and ticking to 10% from 21:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays in the low band so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to ease from 45% to about 41% through the thin Saturday Gulf, Asian and European hours, when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 45-46% into the late slots as unresolved threads - the Hormuz impasse, the U.S. economic-isolation package flagged for next week, the Iran-Oman shipping talks and the Novorossiysk export halt - converge on Sunday's price discovery. Confidence stays in the medium-low band at 56-59% for as long as no venue quotes. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way and the first live tape, not this forecast, is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.
